MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
  MARCH 26, 2019

An adjourned regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 4:05 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR
MITCHELL.

2.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff*, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman.
  *Arrived at 4:15 p.m.
City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Attorney Kane Thuyen
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

3.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Leonard Pagarigan, 63 Hidden Valley Road addressed the City Council to encourage the City to
include the Palos Verdes Symphonic Band (PVSB) as a paid performer at the 2019 City Celebration
in September and consider designating the PVSB as the community band for the City with equitable
annual sponsorship.

Suzy Seamans, 1 Peacock Lane addressed the City Council in support of Mr. Pagarigan’s request.
Ms. Seamans also encouraged the City to consider increasing the City’s grant funding amount for
HOAs wishing to improve their entryway.

Paul Moilanen, 31 Hitching Post Drive addressed the City Council to express concern regarding
traffic safety at the intersection of Hitching Post Drive/Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes
Drive North/Palos Verdes Drive East; and the potential negative impacts to the Hitching Post
Neighborhood from increased vehicular traffic and usage of the proposed Nature Center. Mr.
Moilanen further suggested that the City improve neighborhood communication regarding impactful
projects and continue to engage the public.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MARCH 26, 2019 (PDS)
 4.  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

A.  MID-YEAR REPORTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file these reports.

  The Mid-Year status reports were presented for City Council consideration. MAYOR PRO
  TEM SCHMITZ commented that Special Events and the Pepper Tree Foundation reports
  have the same first paragraph. Community Services Director Clark noted that was a
  typographical error in the report.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE MID-YEAR REPORTS.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR MITCHELL SO ORDERED

B.  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION ITEMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council consider the items presented and prioritize them
  on the work plan for the coming fiscal year.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material) and
  requested the Council’s input on the following items:

  EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS: Equine Preparedness Subcommittee

  Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that the Equestrian Committee’s Equine
  Preparedness Subcommittee in its discussions regarding emergency preparedness is
  suggesting that the City establish a cache of emergency supplies for equestrian-specific
  needs.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF commented that the subcommittee developed a list of
  suggested items. Community Services Director Clark reviewed the list noting that it is
  proposed that the items be stored at various parks through the City including Dapplegray
  Park, Ernie Howlett Park and the Peter Weber Equestrian Center. Council discussed the
  items and weighed the pros and cons of the City providing the supplies noting that it may
  not be a good to include perishable food. It was further suggested that the supplies could
  possibly be purchased through the Pepper Tree Foundation.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  work with the subcommittee to develop a list of supplies and proposed locations
  and bring back to the City Council for consideration as part of the budget process.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 26, 2019 (PDS)
   COUNCILMEMBER HUFF noted that the subcommittee has also been discussing the
  possibility of conducting a horse census to help gauge the needs of the equestrian
  community based on the number of horses in the city.

  Administrative Analyst Slawson reviewed the draft horse census and discussed the
  options for conducting the census. MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ commented that having
  the data for the horse census would allow the COUNCIL to make a more informed
  decision regarding equine emergency supplies. Discussion ensued concerning the
  importance of obtaining census data for all horses including boarded horses.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  proceed with conducting the horse census.

  MARLOMA SEWER STUDY

  Assistant City Manager Grammer reviewed the staff report (as per the agenda material)
  noting that in working with the Marloma Home Owners Association, there seems to be
  preliminary interest in moving forward with a sewer assessment district and they are
  requesting that the City help with providing some of the upfront costs. He noted that
  Willdan estimates that cost for the preliminary design, engineers report and balloting
  would be approximately $125,000, which would be reimbursed if the sewer assessment
  district is approved.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that the City may want to consider a more
  widespread effort to address this issue in other areas of the city that are also still on septic
  systems and possibly use the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District (EIFD) process
  to fund a project community wide.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  further explore other financing options and talk to other neighborhoods.

  Assistant City Manager noted that if the Marloma Neighborhood decides to move forward,
  the matter will be brought back to the City Council for further discussion.

  MUNICIPAL STORMWATER PROGRAM

  Assistant City Manager Grammer reviewed the staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that the City reach out to Assembly Member
  Muratsuchi to request that he host another meeting with the South Bay cities to discuss
  stormwater issues and the costs cities are faced with in complying with these mandated
  regulations.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  contact Assembly Member Muratsuchi’s office to schedule a meeting to discuss
  stormwater management issues.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 26, 2019 (PDS)
   PUBLIC OUTREACH

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).
  John Barilone with Tripepi Smith reviewed a PowerPoint presentation providing an
  overview of the City’s strategic communications plan and public outreach efforts over the
  last year including the analytics associated with those efforts.

  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that Tripepi Smith, in conjunction with staff and
  with input from the Park & Activities Commission, has created an updated logo for the
  Pepper Tree Foundation; and presented the updated logo for the City Council’s review
  and input.

  Discussion ensued concerning the logo design. COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN
  suggested incorporating a three-rail fence and anchoring the horse to the design. It was
  also noted that the white walkway looks out of place. Assistant to the City Manager Davis
  provided background on the previous versions and how it got to this stage.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer further stated that as part of the rebranding of the
  Pepper Tree Foundation, staff believes there is an opportunity to increase fundraising
  efforts and build a more robust nonprofit organization to fund larger scale projects. In that
  vein, the City may want to consider establishing a community committee to guide such
  an effort.

  Discussion ensued concerning the opportunities for enhancing the Pepper Tree
  Foundation as a non-profit organization.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council that it would be
  beneficial to pursue updating the Pepper Tree Foundation bylaws to allow for more
  robust fundraising activities and to create a development committee.

  At 5:45 p.m. the MAYOR MITCHELL called for a brief recess.

  MAYOR MITCHELL called the meeting back to order at 5:55 p.m. with all
  Councilmembers present.

  PLANNING DIRECTOR

  MAJOR PROJECT UPDATES

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material) on the status
  of the City’s major development projects.

  Discussion ensued concerning the Brickwalk/Slide Area Project and the Rolling Hills
  Country Club project including demolition of the old clubhouse building. Senior Planner
  Naughton explained that the Environmental Impact Report generated during the

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 26, 2019 (PDS)
   entitlement process does not contemplate the traffic impacts if the structure were to
  remain and any future use would require additional environmental studies.

  Recognizing that there were members of the public present to address the coyote fencing
  matter, Assistant City Manager Grammer suggested pausing the major project update
  discussion and moving to the coyote fencing matter.

  COYOTE FENCING

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report regarding coyote fencing (as per the
  agenda material) and reviewed a PowerPoint presentation of what other neighboring
  cities allow and what type of fencing the County recommends to reduce the likelihood of
  a coyote gaining access to a property. He further provided some examples of fences that
  have been constructed in the City recently to prevent coyotes from entering a property,
  many of which include outward protrusions. Administrative Analyst Slawson noted the
  County has expressed concern regarding fences with outward protrusions in that they
  could make it difficult for firefighters to access a property in the case of an emergency
  and that the protrusions could trap a coyote inside a property causing additional risk.

  Following the presentation, Planning Director Wahba stated that staff is seeking the City
  Council’s direction as to whether or not the City should make any changes to its fencing
  regulations to address these issues.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN noted that the protrusions could be problematic in
  situations where they protrude into someone else’s property or into city easements.

  Dr. Troy Wilson, 5 Ponderosa Lane addressed the City Council and provided
  photographic examples of fences that have been installed that do not meet the City’s
  current fencing regulations. He expressed concern that these types of fences are not
  consistent with the City’s rural, equestrian environment and open views. He showed
  examples of where the fences can turn into wall like structures resulting in blocked views
  and reduced open space. Dr. Wilson urged the City Council not to amend its ordinance
  to allow for taller fencing.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that he sees both sides of this issue and
  the City also needs to be cognizant of people’s fear.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that he also sees both sides of this issue
  and feels for the residents who have lost pets due to coyotes. He further commented that
  City needs to develop policy that helps its residents but he would not want to change what
  the City currently allows regarding fencing at this time. He felt the matter could be
  discussed further over time.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ commented that rural environments include nature and the
  raccoons are also dangerous. She further commented that the City should not make
  policy out of fear and suggested that the City continue to educate its residents.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 26, 2019 (PDS)
   MAYOR MITCHELL commented that she is concerned about the long-term effects on the
  look of the community that these types of fences will effectuate.

  Discussion ensued concerning the way residents can protect their pets including
  supervising their pets when outside and constructing dog runs when they can’t supervise
  their pets.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council not to amend the
  City’s municipal code regarding fencing at this time and to direct staff to pursue
  code enforcement on the cases it is aware of currently; and then on a complaint
  basis moving forward.

  METROPOLITAN WATER DISTRICT USE OF THE CORNER AT PVDN AND PVDE

  Planning Director Wahba provided an overview of Metropolitan Water District’s (MWD’s)
  reservoir project (as per the agenda material) noting that because of this upcoming
  project, it may make sense to hold off on the development of “Butcher” Park given that
  the MWD project will impact the area significantly.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that he has had previous discussions with
  MWD about allowing for a public use of a portion of the reservoir site so that the City will
  have a consistent look and feel at all four corners of that intersection.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ commented on the continued delays in developing the park
  at “Butcher” corner. Discussion ensued concerning the best way to move forward given
  the complexity and timing of the MWD project.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer also noted that the paving project in the northbound
  lane on Palos Verdes Drive East will also be postponed while MWD is working in the
  roadway and staff will work with MWD to provide funding for paving of that section of
  roadway when the project is complete.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to hold off on the
  development of the park at the corner of PVDN and PVDE while the MWD project is
  ongoing and to work collaboratively with MWD to develop the park and a public
  use at the reservoir site after the MWD project is complete.

  GENERAL PLAN

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ commented that there has been a decline in the service
  provided by Dyett & Bhatia since the departure of key personnel. She noted that she and
  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN along with staff met with the consultant in an effort to
  remedy the service issues. She further commented that the discussions amongst the
  committee members at the General Plan Advisory Committee meetings have been robust
  and varied; and the committee members seem vested in the process.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MARCH 26, 2019 (PDS)
   Discussion ensued concerning the commercial district and ways to incorporate additional
  housing to help the City meet its Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) numbers.
  Further discussion ensued concerning workforce housing and the pros and cons of
  implementing an inclusionary ordinance.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff, in
  conjunction with the City Attorney’s office, to develop an inclusionary ordinance
  for consideration.

  LICENSE AGREEMENT FEE FOR USE OF PUBLIC PROPERTY

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNICLMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that in situations where the issuance of
  license agreement benefits the community and enhances the equestrian nature of the
  community, the fee should be left the same.

  Discussion ensued concerning the current license agreement fee and the pros and cons
  of raising the fee.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  conduct further research as to what would be an appropriate amount to increase
  the license agreement fee and bring back to the City Council for consideration.

  PARKING REQUIREMENTS IN NON-RESIDENTIAL DISTRICTS

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Discussion ensued concerning the City’s current parking requirements and the pros and
  cons of reducing those requirements.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  conduct a study to consider making changes to the parking requirements in non-
  residential districts.

  MEDICAL USES WITHIN SHOPPING CENTERS IN THE COMMERCIAL-GENERAL
  ZONE

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to not amend the
  Zoning Code requirements regarding medical uses within shopping centers in the
  commercial-general zone at this time but rather, continue to discuss this issue
  through the Commercial District Ad Hoc Committee.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
MARCH 26, 2019 (PDS)
   ART DEDICATION REQUIREMENT FOR NEW LARGE PROJECTS OR AN “IN-LIEU”
  FEE

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to not move forward
  with an art dedication fee at this time.

  CITY ATTORNEY PLANNING DEPARTMENT ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Discussion ensued concerning wireless facilities and the need for 5G service in the
  community.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff, in
  conjunction with the City Attorney’s office to prepare updates to the following
  Zoning Code chapters: Personal Wireless Service Facilities (Chapter 17.39) and
  Signs (Chapter 17.60); and to further review the appeal procedures in the Zoning
  Code for consistency.

  ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIRECTOR

  MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead presented the mid-year budget review staff
  report (as per the agenda material).

  FISCAL HEALTH REPORT

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead presented the fiscal health report (as per the
  agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE FISCAL HEALTH REPORT.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR MITCHELL SO ORDERED

  COMMUNITY SERVICES DIRECTOR

  NEW PARK NAME

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8
MARCH 26, 2019 (PDS)
   Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to keep the process
  for naming facilities as is but to keep the City Council informed as the naming
  process progresses.

  PVDN MEDIAN AND PARKWAY MASTER LANDSCAPE PLAN

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to continue to have
  staff review median landscaping as needs arise and bring the item back for City
  Council consideration during the budget process.

  LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to maintain the
  services of Bennet Landscape for landscape maintenance for an additional five
  years and direct staff to prepare an updated agreement.

  NATURE CENTER REPLACEMENT STUDY UPDATE

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Discussion ensued concerning the comments made by the public specifically regarding
  the ingress and egress of the facility and the funding options for developing project.

5.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:57 p.m. MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular
  meeting of the City Council scheduled for Tuesday, April 9, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the
  Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
  Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  9
MARCH 26, 2019 (PDS)
